title: A visual tool astronauts use to assess their own health and act on its status
done_when: The astronaut sees the status of each indicator they track and what to do next, on one screen

title: Gather health indicators from user input: keyboard and clicks; camera or images are optional
done_when: Every chosen indicator can be entered without special hardware; units shown at entry

title: Choose the indicators on purpose, each confirmed measurable on board with a source
done_when: docs/DECISIONS.md lists each indicator, how it is measured in flight and the source; any example from the statement that is left out (for example blood sugar) says why
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (background: blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep hours, mood)

title: Each indicator answers the five questions of the statement
done_when: Measurable in space and how; why needed; hazard effects; when it needs attention; prevention. Each answer sourced or marked Assumption

title: Say when a result needs attention from the crew, the CMO or the flight surgeon
done_when: Each indicator has an attention rule with its source, or the rule is labelled Assumption in the interface

title: Guidance on treatments and health improvement, never a diagnosis
done_when: Every attention state shows what to do; no diagnostic wording or risk percentages anywhere

title: Explain how the five spaceflight hazards affect what is measured
done_when: Each indicator names the hazards that affect it (radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile closed environments) with a NASA source

title: Simple instructions on measurements, indicators and risks; no assumed expertise
done_when: Numbered steps, one action per sentence; Bio 2 reviews every text for plain language

title: Optional considerations chosen or left out on purpose
done_when: Human figure, colour coding, dynamic charts, routine prompts, gamification, mission environments, animations and camera input each have a row in docs/DECISIONS.md: use or leave out, and why
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (objectives and potential considerations)

title: Every medical statement has a source or is marked Assumption, visible to the user
done_when: A reviewer finds no unsourced statement in config/ or the interface; Assumption labels show in the app

title: Never presented as a replacement for the CMO or the flight surgeon
done_when: Interface, pitch and page say the tool supports the crew's own assessment and that decisions stay with the CMO and flight surgeon
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 3004] in-mission medical care)

title: Show how indicators change over time against the person's own earlier values
done_when: Each indicator has a history view; the comparison uses that astronaut's own earlier values
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 3004] trending vital signs; limits relative to each person's baseline) · CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (dynamic charts)

title: Work with delayed or no contact with Earth
done_when: The app and its data keep working with no network; anything for the ground waits and is sent later
source: CS: Challenge statement · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/ (hazard: distance from Earth) · https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/

title: Treat health data as private; the demo uses synthetic data only and says so
done_when: No real personal data anywhere; the interface labels the data as synthetic
source: Our: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C · https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf ([V1 6003] private medical communication)

title: Readable and usable without colour alone or a mouse
done_when: Every state has text or an icon besides colour; the demo path works by keyboard
source: Our: team quality rule (colour coding is a statement consideration)

title: Everything submitted is in English
done_when: Page, app, slides and linked materials in English; a video may be spoken in another language only with English subtitles

title: Demo: video of 30 s or less with English subtitles, or 7 slides at most including title and intro
done_when: Length or slide count checked; hosted outside Space Apps; the link opens with no password, permission or registration

title: Public link to the final project
done_when: Repository and running app open in a private window with no login

title: Use and name at least one NASA data or resource; list every other data, tool, code and image used
done_when: Page fields NASA Data and Space Agency Partner Data filled from docs/nasa_data.md and docs/sources.md; licences and permissions checked
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (required for global awards)

title: Super Intelligence (SI) tools used as the guide allows and disclosed
done_when: The solution idea comes from the team, not from SI tools; the page answers the SI question; SI images and video carry a visible watermark; SI code, data and audio are acknowledged in descriptive text and metadata; no NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers in generated content
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (Use of Super Intelligence)

title: Pitch and page answer the five judging criteria
done_when: Script and page say how the project serves Impact, Creativity, Validity, Relevance and Presentation

title: No images, video, audio or likeness of people under 18
done_when: Every image and clip checked before upload

title: Submit for judging before the internal freeze
done_when: Terms and originality boxes checked and Submit for Judging pressed by Sun 13:30; official close Sun 15 Nov 23:59 Medellín time
source: SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (submission start and end times)

title: All five members registered for the Medellín event and on the team's Members tab
done_when: Members tab of ReTardis shows all five; no member can be added after submission closes
source: JG: Judging guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/judging-awards-guide/ (eligibility: at most six members, same local event)

title: Local judging and the 14:00 mentor presentation confirmed with the local lead and rehearsed
done_when: Time, length and language confirmed (T-04); two-minute story rehearsed three times
source: Local: Medellín event schedule · SG: Submission guide · https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/resources/project-submission-guide/ (local judging times may differ)
